Calculate requires the run to be Prepared (or Calculated with recalculate=true); an already-Calculated run without recalculate is Conflict

Recalculation additionally logs RecalculationRequested and RecalculationCompleted history events around the ordinary Started/Completed pair

Attendance integration: a missing Attendance period is treated as legacy-compatible (calculation proceeds with no snapshot); an existing-but-not-Closed period is AttendanceNotFinalized; a Closed period with no current snapshot is AttendanceSnapshotMissing
An Overtime snapshot resolution failure surfaces as a per-employee CalculationFailed error rather than aborting the whole run
Off-Cycle/Supplementary runs skip the full structure walk entirely and calculate ONLY adjustments plus statutory deductions (CalculateAdjustmentOnlyAsync)
More than one overlapping Active salary assignment for the same employee/period is a CalculationFailed error requiring segmented calculation, not a silent pick
A structure version with zero active components is a NoSalaryStructureVersion error

CalculateValue applies the same FixedAmount/Percentage/Formula/Manual matrix as structure validation, with an active EmployeeSalaryComponent override taking precedence over the structure default (Source=EmployeeOverride vs Structure)
A Percentage component's base must already have been calculated earlier in sequence order, else MissingBaseComponent

Any computed component value below zero is rejected unconditionally as InvalidOverride ('Negative component values are not supported by the generic engine') - there is no supported way for a structure component itself to net negative

Proration: a proratable component whose payable window (assignment/DOJ/DOL-truncated) is shorter than the full period is scaled by payableDays/totalDays; a component whose calculation already referenced an upstream prorated base is NOT prorated a second time
MinimumAmount/MaximumAmount clamps are applied AFTER proration, not before

Approved overtime is added as a synthetic OVERTIME earning using a weighted-minutes formula (Normal/WeekOff/Holiday multipliers) against the resolved hourly-rate base, only when a monthly work-minutes basis is present
Gross/Deductions/Net and every component amount are rounded via PayrollRoundingPolicy.RoundMoney (2 decimal places, MidpointRounding.AwayFromZero, not banker's rounding) at every accumulation step
Negative net pay after the structure walk is a NegativeNetPay error; it is checked AGAIN after statutory deductions are layered in, since statutory alone can also push net below zero

Approved/Scheduled adjustments targeting this run (or the run's period with no specific run) are applied as synthetic components; a deducting adjustment that would exceed available net is rejected with a per-adjustment message naming the AdjustmentNumber

Applied adjustment components are persisted as PayrollAdjustmentApplication rows and the source PayrollAdjustment's Status becomes Applied/PartiallyApplied - but ONLY once the whole employee's calculation succeeds (a rolled-back attempt applies nothing)

Statutory calculation (StatutoryPayrollService.CalculateAsync) layers its EmployeeAmount into TotalDeductions and EmployerAmount into EmployerContributions, recomputes NetPay, and a StatutoryCalculationFailed error aborts just that employee

Loan recovery integration: DeferInstallment skips silently; RecoverFullOrFail blocks the whole employee's calculation if the due installment exceeds available net pay; every other policy clamps the recovered amount down to available net pay

Loan recoveries persist LoanRepayment rows and update LoanInstallment/EmployeeLoan outstanding balances ONLY after the whole run's calculation attempt fully succeeds (a second, post-loop persistence pass)
Reimbursement recoveries add taxable/non-taxable earning components and INCREASE Gross Earnings and Net Pay - unlike loan recoveries and deducting adjustments, this money flows toward the employee
Reimbursement settlements are persisted as ReimbursementSettlement rows (grouped per claim line) and the source claim's SettledAmount/Status are updated, ONLY on full calculation success
GetResults/GetResult/GetErrors read paths are scoped to IsCurrent=true rows only, so a superseded calculation attempt's stale results/errors never surface

A cross-tenant run id on calculate/recalculate/results/errors is NotFound

List/filter payroll adjustments (employeeId, status, adjustmentType, direction) with paging

Exactly one adjustment may exist per (SourceType, SourceId) pair - a duplicate is Conflict
AdjustmentNumber is allocated from a per-tenant-per-year sequence row (PADJ/{year}/{seq:D6}) that retries up to 8 times on a concurrency/insert race rather than relying on provider-specific SQL

Creating a correction adjustment against an OriginalPayrollResultId captures an IMMUTABLE PayrollCorrectionSnapshot (original vs corrected gross/deduction/net) at creation time - it is never recomputed afterward
Submit moves Draft -> Submitted; Approve moves Submitted -> Approved and invokes PayrollApprovalGuard's self-approval block; Reject moves Submitted -> Rejected and requires a reason
Cancel is allowed from Draft OR Submitted (uniquely permissive among the transitions) and requires a reason
History is append-only across Created/CorrectionSnapshotCaptured/Submitted/Approved/Rejected/Cancelled/Applied/PartiallyApplied/Scheduled events

Self-service /api/me/payroll-adjustments* is strictly scoped to the caller's own linked EmployeeId - detail/history routes re-check ownership and return NotFound (not Forbidden) for another employee's adjustment

Off-cycle run creation requires RunType to be OffCycle or Supplementary, else Invalid

Selecting existing adjustments into a new off-cycle run requires every one to be Approved and not already scheduled to a run, atomically within one DB transaction; a mid-flight race rolls the whole run-creation back

Off-cycle Prepare/Approve are thin aliases for the ordinary run Prepare/Transition(Approved) operations
Process orchestrates the full Draft->Prepare->Calculate->Approve->Finalize sequence in one call, short-circuiting from whatever stage the run is already at

PayslipNumber is PS/{yyyyMM}/{employeeId:N}/{version}, with Version incrementing per employee per run on each regeneration

Payslip lines include every structure/adjustment/overtime/reimbursement PayrollResultComponent AND separate statutory lines (DisplayGroup='Statutory Deductions', IsStatutory=true) sourced from PayrollStatutoryResults
Publish requires the run to be Approved or Finalized, and bulk-moves every Generated payslip for the run to Published
Get/GetRunPayslips/GetDocument each accept a publishedOnly flag - the self-service (/api/me/payslips) surface always forces it true
Self-service GetOwnAsync resolves the caller's employee identity and returns only Published payslips for that employee
GetDocument renders a self-contained HTML payslip with every employee/component text field HTML-encoded
The payroll register is paged, searchable by employee code/first/last name, and scoped to IsCurrent results only

List/filter claims (employeeId, categoryId, status, settlementMethod, date range) and get a single claim/history
Create requires at least one line, each with a description and a positive claimed amount, and ExpenseToDate>=ExpenseFromDate

Every line's category must be active and tenant-scoped; a category not flagged AllowsMultipleLines rejects a second line in the same category; every line's category currency must match the claim's CurrencyCode

ClaimNumber is CLM/{yyyy}/{seq:000000}, computed by scanning the max existing suffix for the tenant/year rather than a dedicated sequence row - unlike PayrollAdjustment's dedicated, retry-safe PayrollAdjustmentNumberSequence
ReconcileClaim recomputes claim-level TotalClaimedAmount/EligibleAmount/ApprovedAmount/TaxableAmount/NonTaxableAmount from the current line set on every mutation

Submit resolves an active policy per line's ExpenseDate (else Invalid), computes EligibleAmount from the policy's PerTransactionLimit/MaxClaimAmount/MinClaimAmount, and requires every receipt-required line to already have an uploaded receipt
Submit requires the claiming employee to still be Active

Approve (maker-checker) only fires from Submitted/UnderReview; each line's ApprovedAmount is bounded 0..EligibleAmount, splits Taxable/NonTaxable per the policy's TaxTreatment (or an explicit override), and the claim's overall status is derived (Rejected/PartiallyApproved/promoted straight to ReadyForSettlement)

Attachment metadata (filename/contentType/storageReference/non-negative size) is validated, and attaching to a specific line flips that line's ReceiptStatus to Uploaded

API: n/a (service-level; no dedicated controller route was found)

Functionality: Self-service /api/me/reimbursements* re-checks ownership (EmployeeId match) on detail/update/submit/attachment/history, returning NotFound for another employee's claim

CreateRetroCase requires EffectiveTo>=EffectiveFrom and an existing tenant employee

CONFIRMED CODE-LEVEL DEFECT: EvaluateRetroAsync hardcodes every snapshot's CorrectedGross/CorrectedDeductions/CorrectedNet EQUAL to the original amount with GrossDifference/DeductionDifference/NetDifference all fixed at 0 - it never recalculates anything. Because Status only becomes Evaluated when at least one result has a nonzero NetDifference, and every row's NetDifference is unconditionally 0, a retro case can NEVER reach Evaluated - it always lands on NoImpact, even when a real, intended correction exists
ApproveRetro is consequently unreachable through ordinary use, since it requires Status=Evaluated (CR-181's finding) and invokes the approval guard's self-approval block
ApplyRetro requires Status=Approved and a target run in Draft/Prepared; each nonzero-difference component becomes a pre-Scheduled ArrearEarning/ArrearDeduction PayrollAdjustment
Implementation Status: Implemented (unreachable precondition, same root cause as CR-181)

GrossPayable/TotalDeductions/NetSettlement are fully recomputed from ALL lines (manual + generated) on every Calculate call, not just the newly-generated ones

Approve requires Calculated status and the approval guard's self-approval check; Finalize requires Approved and rejects a negative NetSettlement (re-confirms qa/09-separation's CR-157 - the SAME check, on the SAME shared service, from the Payroll module's own perspective)

Finalize is the ONLY point where the sub-ledger side-effects actually post: LoanRepayment rows (idempotent per settlement id), ReimbursementSettlement rows (SettlementType=FinalSettlement, idempotent per line+settlement), VariablePaySettlement rows, and PayrollAdjustmentApplication rows are all created here, never at Calculate time

A cross-tenant retro-case/final-settlement id is NotFound

Validate re-checks every line fresh each call (clearing prior issues) against: EMPLOYEE_NOT_FOUND, EMPLOYEE_INACTIVE (warning-only), COMPONENT_NOT_FOUND, COMPONENT_NOT_EFFECTIVE, INVALID_COMPONENT_TYPE, INVALID_AMOUNT, PERIOD_FINALIZED, and DUPLICATE_ROW
Batch status becomes ValidationFailed if any line is Invalid after validation, else Validated
Preview aggregates earning/deduction totals, employee count, and component count while excluding Invalid lines
Editing or deleting a staged line downgrades the WHOLE batch back to Draft and resets its validation counts, forcing a fresh Validate
Submit is Validated-only and is blocked while InvalidRows>0
Approve is Submitted-only and invokes the approval guard's self-approval block; Reject requires a reason and is Submitted-only

Post is Approved-only with InvalidRows==0, converts each non-InformationOnly line into a PayrollAdjustment inside a Serializable transaction, and is idempotent per line (a retried Post after partial failure never double-creates an adjustment for an already-posted line)

Cancel on a Posted batch is blocked once any PayrollAdjustmentApplication already exists for it ('Finalized Payroll may not be rewritten; submit this correction through Phase 7R'), else bulk-cancels its still-unapplied generated adjustments; otherwise Cancel works from Draft/Validated/ValidationFailed/Approved/Posted
History is append-only across Created/Uploaded/Validated/ValidationFailed/Corrected/Submitted/Approved/Rejected/Posted/Cancelled events

Manager holds ZERO Payroll permissions of any kind - there is no seeded way for a manager to see even their own direct reports' payroll data through this module

SuperHR is directly seeded (not merely self-escalated) with a PARTIAL native payroll footprint - full Salary Component/Structure/Employee-Salary management, Period management+Unlock, Controls management, and Run management including Run.Approve/Run.Finalize/Run.Calculate/Run.Recalculate - broader than HRManager's footprint of literally zero

API: GET/PUT/POST across every in-scope Payroll controller

Every history/audit table discovered in this module (SalaryComponentHistories, SalaryStructureHistories, EmployeeSalaryAssignmentHistories, PayrollPeriodHistories, PayrollRunHistories, PayrollCalculationHistories, PayrollAdjustmentHistories, PayslipHistories, ReimbursementHistories, PayrollRetroHistories, FinalSettlementHistories, PayrollInputHistories) is written via an Add-only call pattern - no Update/Remove call against any *History DbSet was found anywhere in the read source
Service: every in-scope *Service.cs AddHistory method (grep for db.*Histories.Update / .Remove)

Functionality: Every history row captures ActorUserId from the current tenant context at the moment of the mutation, giving a reliable who-did-it trail even though no dedicated single unified payroll audit log table exists

Every PayrollReportsController route shares exactly ONE controller-level permission (Payroll.Analytics.View) - the payroll register, bank-payments, and statutory-summary reports are all gated identically, with no finer per-report split
